_note: DQ-T30 — a question naming stored data must be answered from a tool call in THIS turn. The MEASURED turn is the LAST one: turn 1 is the setup that succeeded live on 2026-08-13, and the RE-ASK is what failed. A single-turn scenario would record turn 1 as a clean pass and never see the defect.

scenarios.prompt: What canon rules have I declared for this book?
follow_ups: Remind me again — what canon rules do I have on this book right now?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['canon rules'] — the author's exact words on the measured turn

args.text: Magic always costs lifespan — every spell burns years from the caster.
The Obsidian Trench never appears on two maps at once.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM canon_rule WHERE project_id='{project_id}' AND active
seed_assert.why: TWO rules must exist, because the measured failure is a COUNT: the re-ask answered 'one rule'. With one rule seeded, a stale answer and a correct answer are the same sentence and the scenario proves nothing.

answer_expect.why: Both seeded rules must appear in the answer to the RE-ASK. The measured failure named one and invented the other, so a reply carrying only one rule is the defect reproducing, not a partial pass.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the re-ask (the LAST turn) answers without composition_list_canon_rules appearing in that turn's tool calls, OR the reply states a count or a rule text that is not in the store, OR a read-intent turn changes the store. CONTROL: turn 1 is recorded in prior_turns — if turn 1 ALSO failed to call the tool, this scenario is measuring the first-ask path (D-FJ-18's territory) and NOT the staleness DQ-T30 names, so the reading is void.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a book with zero canon rules must answer 'none declared' from a tool call, not from silence.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — the read is project-scoped; a second account must not see these rules.
